## Beacon Overview

Beacon is an open-source memory layer for AI coding agents that learns from your work across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and 20+ other harnesses. It captures full session history, identifies useful workflows, corrections, and debugging patterns, and makes that knowledge reusable by future agents. Built for developers who want agent knowledge to compound across tools instead of disappearing when a session ends.

## 🚀 Quick Start

Beacon is open source and local-first. Interactive endpoint setup signs in through beacon.sh and preselects Beacon Cloud, with an explicit Local opt-out. Signing in forwards nothing; confirming Managed installs Beacon and connects this machine in the same command, and the confirm screen says so before you accept. Setup then ends on a short summary and opens the hosted dashboard at beacon.sh/dashboard. System, package, MDM, and CI installation paths remain noninteractive and account-free.

### 1. Install Beacon

Copy & paste setup prompt into your coding agent

```
Read  then set me up on Beacon 
```

brew update brew trust asymptote-labs/tap brew tap asymptote-labs/tap brew install beacon beacon endpoint install

results.title: Beacon MCP: Self-Improving Memory Layer for Coding Agents | Justin D. posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content:
Yesterday we launched the next chapter of our open source project Beacon by Asymptote Labs. The response has been wild. We more than doubled our GitHub stars in 12 hours. But the most exciting part has been seeing how strongly the core idea resonates: Your agent history should compound, not disappear when a session ends. Beacon is an open-source memory layer for AI coding agents. It captures session history across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and 20+ other harnesses, then turns the best workflows, corrections, debugging patterns, and repo knowledge into reusable memory for future agents. That means: Claude Code can teach Codex. Cursor debugging can improve OpenCode. A correction you make once can help every agent you use next. And because Beacon sits across the harness layer, [...] You've run thousands of agent sessions. Your agents remember none of them. Beacon by Asymptote Labs is an open-source, self-improving memory layer for coding agents. Our latest release ships Beacon MCP: blazing-fast search over petabytes of session history, available to any agent in any harness: → Claude Code → Codex → Cursor → OpenCode and 20+ more GitHub repo:  (don't forget to star it ⭐) Beacon captures every agent session you run. The problem is that your next agent can't see any of them. Beacon MCP fixes that with one command: beacon mcp connect It finds your harnesses and wires Beacon into each one. Sign-in is OAuth, so no API keys end up in your config files. Now every agent can: → search every past session → grep everything your agents have ever done → pull up the exact command [...] + Report this post

  The AI security stack is looking in the wrong place. After watching how enterprises are adopting local agents, my cofounder Shukan and I have developed a strongly held belief at Asymptote Labs: Local agents move the security boundary from the gateway to the endpoint. Gateways can tell you what a model saw or said. They cannot tell you what a local agent actually did inside a user’s work environment: which tools it used, what it touched, what changed, and what was approved. That is the visibility gap we built Beacon to close. Beacon is the world’s first open-source endpoint telemetry layer for local AI agents. Agent activity has to become observable before it can become governable. Open source. MIT licensed. Read the launch post. Star the repo.

We found no good free alternatives out there, so we built our own and fully open-sourced it!

Beacon hooks into 20+ different agent harnesses, captures session telemetry (prompts, tool calls, command executions, etc) in one normalized format, and distills it into common patterns and repeatable workflows with a human-approval step. This compounded knowledge is then accessible to any future agent via skills / MCP.

We believe your agent data is yours to own and should not be locked behind any frontier lab's ecosystem or closed memory infrastructure. We built Beacon to make working across agents way more transparent and efficient.
